The First World War and the collapse of the empires gave Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia their first opportunity to build independent states, and left them in ruins. The German advance of 1915 stabilised along the Daugava, within reach of Riga, for two and a half years; the imperial government evacuated Latvia's industry eastwards, and most of it never returned; Riga lost more than half its population between 1914 and 1919

when the pre-war level was regained. The new states rebuilt on the land.
